subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw handle this crash class with a narrow Playwright assertion classifier, a browser-profile connection quarantine/reconnect boundary, or a larger browser/CDP subprocess isolation design?
rationale: All options can reduce the crash, but they differ in how much unknown Playwright state OpenClaw suppresses, how sessions recover, and whether browser failures stay in the main Gateway process.

options.title: Design browser isolation/recovery first
options.body: Keep this issue open and have a browser/Gateway owner specify the crash boundary, recovery semantics, and live proof requirements before implementation.

options.title: Accept a narrow classifier
options.body: Treat only well-identified Playwright CDP assertion shapes as non-fatal while keeping unknown unhandled rejections fatal.

options.title: Defer until live repro
options.body: Wait for a current-main CRSession repro before choosing any code path, leaving the production crash report open as tracking context.

recommendation.title: Design browser isolation/recovery first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have a browser/Gateway owner specify the crash boundary, recovery semantics, and live proof requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across browser CDP, bundled browser plugin ownership, and the unhandled-rejection safety surface.
